# Decompression amplification

A zlib importer limits compressed input to 1024 bytes but inflates without an output limit. Small compressed inputs exceed the intended 1024-byte expanded-data budget and are written to a real file. Catalog attack outputs are limited to 4096 bytes.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Technology | Python |
| CWE | CWE-409 |
| OWASP | A06:2025 |
| Test scope | `executable` |

[Vulnerable source](vulnerable/main.py) · [Corrected source](fixed/main.py)

## Correction

Use the decoder output limit to allocate at most the budget plus one detection byte. Reject oversized output before publication, and require one complete stream with no trailing data. Tests verify actual output bytes and the decoder allocation bound. This is a single-stream local model; archive recursion and sustained service-level exhaustion are outside scope.

## Regression

```sh
python3 tools/lab.py test --case python/decompression-amplification --strict
```

Run from the repository root. Exact inputs and expected outputs are in
[the catalog](../../../catalog/cases.json). Both variants are tested.

The runner also checks every declared file effect. `functional` vectors can specify a useful
operation that the vulnerable implementation did not support correctly; `robustness` vectors
exercise malformed inputs. `benign` vectors require identical expectations.

## Inspiration and provenance

Original benchmark implementation inspired by the documented weakness;
no third-party exploit source is copied or executed.

- [MITRE CWE-409 — Data Amplification](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html)
- [Python zlib decompression objects](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zlib.html#decompression-objects)

This example demonstrates the declared weakness within the documented fixture assumptions.
It is not a production application or a proof that every related attack is prevented.
